codes.DEV: AI benefits or applications for development, SDGs, public services, productivity or innovation
codes.ACCESS: Unequal access or benefits; capacity, infrastructure, data, compute, finance or technology transfer
codes.GOV: International AI rules, governance institutions, coordination, treaties, standards or inclusive rule-making
codes.SAFETY: AI risks, safety, trustworthiness or human oversight, including existential risks
codes.RIGHTS: AI ethics, human rights, discrimination, dignity, privacy or protection of children
codes.SECURITY: Military AI, autonomous weapons, peace and security, AI-enabled crime or cyber threats
codes.INFO: AI misinformation, manipulation, deepfakes, truth or democratic information integrity
codes.WORK: AI effects on jobs, workers, skills or education specifically preparing people to use AI
codes.ENV: AI's environmental footprint or explicit AI applications to climate or environmental problems
codes.POWER: AI concentration, technological sovereignty, dependence or geopolitical competition

rules: Themes require a demonstrated AI connection. Nearby generic digital or SDG content is insufficient.
A speech may receive any number of themes, including zero for a passing AI reference.
GOV is not automatically assigned whenever UN is mentioned.
National programme announcements alone are not international policy demands.
Institutional references are separately coded; generic international cooperation does not imply support for named mechanisms.
Only reviewed source decisions feed final theme statistics. Preserve provisional ASR results separately.
Cluster memberships are not thematic codes.
A theme records attention, including explicit opposition or rejection of a risk narrative; it does not measure support.
Head means incumbent head of state or government; deputies, crown princes and foreign ministers are other. Unknown is retained when identity is not securely established.
Physical PDF pages are one-based; ASR paragraphs are one-based source blocks, not invented PDF pages.
